description.narrative: In the midst of escalating climate breakdown and increasing repression, Climate Weekend 2025 offers a vital moment for collective reflection, strategy, and connection. From May 16 to May 18, approximately 100 climate activists, organizers, and allies will gather for an immersive weekend retreat near Utrecht. This three-day event is not only a space to exchange knowledge and build skills, but also a strategic intervention: a call to reclaim our right to protest.Throughout the weekend, participants will explore the challenges and possibilities facing the climate movement in the Netherlands and beyond. From political analysis to creative expression, and from historical insight to hands-on action planning, the program is designed to strengthen movement-building on multiple levels. Thematically, the weekend centers around the increasing criminalization and limitation of protest, with dedicated sessions on civil liberties, organizing strategies, and collective resilience.Workshops include topics such as the legal dimensions of protest (with Amnesty International), grassroots organizing (led by FNV Young <(>&<)> United), and international perspectives on movement strategy (with Climáximo from Portugal). Other sessions will cover the intersection of climate and militarization, the role of trade unions, andimaginative approaches to storytelling and artistic resistance.In addition to structured sessions, the program provides space for informal networking, shared meals, and artistic activities such as banner-making and musical expression. The entire weekend is hostedin a wheelchair-accessible group accommodation, with vegan meals provided and shared sleeping spaces. For those unable to attend the full weekend, Saturday afternoon offers an open invitation to join a condensed version of the program.By creating space to learn from one another, foster cross-movement solidarity, and imagine bold new strategies, Climate Weekend 2025 stands as a testament to the enduring power of collective action in times of crisis.

participating-org.narrative:
Greenpeace is an independent, international environmental organisation working for a green, peaceful planet.
As a global organisation, Greanpeace focuses on solving the most important environmental problems of our time, the loss of biodiversity and the climate crisis. As explained by the counterpart: To tackle these problems, we need to stop using fossil fuels, protect our forests and oceans and make our agriculture sustainable. Greenpeace is committed worldwide to getting exactly those things done. They research, put items on the agenda, talk to companies and politicians and campaign for real solutions. Together with scientists, environmental organisations and local communities.
Greenpeace Netherlands employs about 100 people and has about 2,000 volunteers. Their managing director is Andy Palmen. They have an independent, unpaid Supervisory Board of expert and experienced people.
